sentences.text: The suit is filed by the plaintiff to declare that the Judgment and Decree passed in O.S.No.10127/2015 dated 28.04.2017 by Hon'ble Addl. City Civil & Sessions Judge, Bengaluru is not binding on the plaintiff nor it is relating to the suit schedule properties and for permanent injunction restraining the defendant, his agents, servants or any persons claiming under him from interfering with plaintiff's peaceful possession and enjoyment of suit schedule properties .

2. The plaintiff's case in brief is as follows :
The plaintiff submits that he is the absolute owner in peaceful possession and enjoyment of Site No.5, 6, 12, 13, 40, 41, 42, 43, 44, 45, 46, 47, 52 & 53 measuring / 4 / O.S.No.1208/2023 East to West 40 feet and North to South 30 feet formed in Sy.No.38/2 of Nagadevanahalli village, Kengeri Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk and described as item Nos.1 to 14 of suit properties.
The said sites are abutting to each other.

Further states, the plaintiff has purchased item Nos.1 to 4 from previous owner Sri.
Veeranna S/o HoosamaneDodaiah under registered Sale Deed dated 05.07.2013.
Whereas, item Nos. 6 to 14 were purchased by the plaintiff's father namely H.Panchanna during his lifetime.
After the demise of plaintiff's father, the plaintiff succeeded to the estate of his father and inherited item Nos.5 to 15 of suit schedule properties.

Further contend that, the plaintiff's mother and sister have executed Nandish M P vs Kumar on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96817976/
2 registered Relinquishment Deed dated 21.08.2015 in favour of the plaintiff in respect of the item Nos.5 to 14 of suit schedule properties.
/ 5 / O.S.No.1208/2023 3.
Further states that, the plaintiff is in peaceful possession and enjoyment of suit schedule properties.

Further contended that, the land bearing Sy.No.38/2 of Nagadevanahalli village, Kengeri Hobli,
Bengaluru South taluk measuring 5 acre 30 guntas was originally owned and possessed by Sri.HosamaneChikkanna.

On 16.02.1993 the legal heirs of Sri.HosamaneChikkanna partitioned the properties and under the said partition, Sri.Veeranna S/o Hosamane Doddaiah got allotted 2 acres 30 guntas and Smt. Chikkamma W/o Yerappa got allotted 2 acres 2 guntas and Sri.Veeranna and Sri.Chikkanna both being sons of Sri.Mooganna jointly got allotted remaining land measuring 24 guntas in Sy.No.38/2 of Nagadevanahalli village.
Further contended that, the revenue records stood in the name of Sri.Veeranna S/o HosamaneDoddaiah as per M.R.No.11/1997-98.

Further submitted that, Sri.Veeranna S/o HosamaneDoddaiah formed residential layout in the Sy.No.38/2 of Nagadevanahalli village to an extent measuring 2 acre 30 guntas out of which item Nos.1 to 14 of suit schedule properties were carved out.
Further stated that, the plaintiff has got 'B' Khatha in his name and paying taxes to the concerned authorities.
The plaintiff has also built watchman shed in some of the suit schedule properties and fenced all the sides.
Further contended that, he has taken Electricity and Water connection to some of the suit schedule properties.

5. Further state, the defendant representing himself as grandson of Smt.Chikkamma W/o Yerappa had / 7 / O.S.No.1208/2023 filed suit in O.S.No.10127/2015 against the BDA which was decreed on 28.04.2017.
Wherein, the defendant was declared to be as absolute owner in possession of suit schedule property to an extent measuring 3 acres in Sy.No.38/2 of Nagadevanahalli village.
The BDA has preferred appeal in R.F.A. No.1689/2017 (Dec/INJ) which is pending for consideration.
6. Further contend, the decree in O.S.No.10127/2015 is limited to an extent of 3 acres and it has nothing to do with item Nos.1 to 14 of suit schedule properties.

The defendant taking advantage of the decree, on 14.02.2023 dictated the plaintiff to demolish the watchman shed and to remove the fence built over the suit schedule properties and threatened that he would interfere with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of / 8 / O.S.No.1208/2023 plaintiff's properties.

The defendant again on 15.02.2023 along with some persons came near the suit schedule properties and interfered with the plaintiff's peaceful possession and enjoyment of the property and the plaintiff gave complaint to Kengeri Police Station.
However, the police advised the plaintiff to approach civil court.
The cause of action for the suit arose on 14.02.2023 and subsequently, when the defendant tried to dispossess the plaintiff and hence, prays for the reliefs as sought for.

The defendant in the written statement apart from usual denial of the plaint averments contend that, the grandmother of the defendant Smt.Chikkamma had acquired land through registered Gift Deed and inheritance measuring 5 acre 30 guntas in Sy.No.38/2 from her late husband Yeraiah who acquired the land in family partition.
Hence, the grandmother of the defendant Smt.Chikkamma was the absolute owner of 5 acre 30 guntas in Sy.No.38/2.
All the revenue records stood in her name.
After the death of Smt.Chikkamma, the defendant being the legal heir became the owner in possession of 5 acre 13 guntas and he is in lawful possession and enjoyment of the said land.
Further state, the alleged Veeranna is not at all the owner and he has no revenue title over the suit land to form the residential layout.

Further contend, Sy.No.38/2 was acquired by BDA in the year 1989 and upon the objections of the alleged vendor of the plaintiff's and others, the BDA had referred the matter under section 30, 31(2) of Land Acquisition Act in LAC 28/1996 before Hon'ble Addl. City civil judge,
Bengaluru.
In the said proceedings, the grandmother of the defendant Smt.Chikkamma appeared as claimant No.4 and the vendor of the plaintiff, Veeranna / 10 / O.S.No.1208/2023 appeared as claimant No.5.

In the said LAC proceedings after full fledged enquiry and after considering the evidence of the claimants, the Hon'ble court allowed the claim of grandmother of the defendant i.e.,
claimant No.4 and rejected the claim of other claimants including the claim of the vendor of the plaintiff and the said judgment and decree was passed on 06.11.2004 and no appeal has been filed against the said judgment and it has attained finality.
8.
Further state, one Smt.Chikkamma, the daughter of Veeranna had filed O.S.No.5501/2022 before this Hon'ble court seeking partition of the property.
In the said suit, the defendant appeared and filed application under Order VII Rule 11 of CPC and the plaint was rejected on merits vide order dated 23.05.2023.
The plaintiff is / 11 / O.S.No.1208/2023 claiming right over the suit property under Veeranna whose claim is rejected in LAC No.28/1996.
Hence, the plaintiff has not acquired any right, title and interest over the suit schedule properties and was never in possession and enjoyment of the same.

9. Further state, the defendant had filed W.P.No.14449/2019 against BDA challenging the acquisition proceedings on the ground that, he is in physical possession of the land and scheme of BDA lapsed due to non-development of acquired land and same is pending for consideration.
The defendant is in physical possession and enjoyment over the said land.
Hence, prays for dismissal of the suit with costs.

In the light of the aforesaid rival pleadings of the parties, the following issues have been framed by my predecessor in office :
(1) Whether the plaintiff proves that he became the absolute owner of item No.1 to 4 of the suit schedule site property by virtue of registered sale deeds dated 05.07.2013 ?

The plaintiff has not acquired any valid right, title and interest in suit schedule properties and was never in possession of the same.

16. The counsel for the plaintiff has argued that, the plaintiff is the owner in possession of the suit schedule / 16 / O.S.No.1208/2023 properties and in support to his contention he has produced a registered Sale Deeds marked as Exs.P1 to 14 and Exs.P15 to 24 are the copies of the Release Deeds and revenue extracts showing that the plaintiff is owner in possession of the suit schedule properties.

the defendant is trying to interfere with the plaintiff's possession of the suit schedule properties.
Hence, prayed for the relief as sought for.

17. The counsel for the defendant submitted that, Veeranna had no title over the suit properties and the sale deeds produced by the plaintiff shows that no consideration is passed under Exs.P.1 to 14.
Further argued / 17 / O.S.No.1208/2023 that, the plaintiff has not produced the GPA copy to show the plaintiff had valid title over the suit schedule properties.

18. The counsel for the defendant relied on the following citations.

sentences.text: Perused the principle laid down in the above said citations.
Wherein it is held that, in the case of transfer of immovable property, if it is executed without payment of price or sale consideration, then it is not a sale at all in the eyes of law.
It is of no legal effect such a sale will be void.

Further it is observed that, revenue entries does not confer any right, title or interest in favour of the person and the mutation entry in the revenue records is only for the fiscal purpose.

He has reiterated the plaint averments in his chief examination by way of affidavit and also deposed that judgment passed Nandish M P vs Kumar on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96817976/

22. As per Ex.P.38, 2.30 guntas stood in the name of Veeranna under Panchayath Parikath out of 5 acres 20 guntas which is reflected in Ex.P39 the RTC extract.
In the / 22 / O.S.No.1208/2023 cross-examination he deposed that, MR and RTC stood in the name of Veeranna but, he does not remember about the khatha extracts.

23. The Defendant examined himself as D.W.1, he has reiterated the written statement averments in his chief examination and got marked Exs.D.1 to 14.
Ex.D.1 is the certified copy of Judgment in LAC No.28/1996 wherein, the judgment was passed on 06.11.2004.
In the said case, the vendor of the plaintiff, Veeranna is shown as claimant No.5 and grandmother of the defendant Smt.Chikkamma shown as claimant No.4.
Said judgment is under Sec.30 & 31(2) of Land Acquisition Act in respect of acquisition of 5 acres 27 guntas in Sy.No.38/2 situated at Nagadevanahalli village, Kengeri Hobli, by the BDA.

The land was acquired by the BDA for formation of Gnanabharathi layout and the preliminary notification was published on 19.01.1989, 26.01.1989 and 02.02.1989 and final notification was / 25 / O.S.No.1208/2023 published on 19.01.1994.
The possession of the acquired land was taken on 31.01.1995.
After recording the evidence of the parties, the Hon'ble court has observed that, the claimant No.5 Veeranna had failed to prove his title over the acquired property.

In page No.6 of the said judgment it is observed that, the claimant No.5 Veeranna who is the son of HosamaneDoddaiah claimed under Panchayath Parikath dated 16.02.1993 2 acres 30 guntas fell to his share in Sy.No.38/2 and the revenue records stood in his name and he is entitled to receive compensation to the extent of 2 acre 30 guntas.

The Hon'ble court after adjudicating the case of the parties has observed that, the claimant No.5 failed to prove he has right, title and interest over 2 acres 30 guntas of the acquired land and said aspect described in Page No.15 of the judgment and it was ordered that the grandmother of the defendant / 26 / O.S.No.1208/2023 Smt.Chikkamma had proved her right, title and interest to the extent of 2 acres 27 guntas in Sy.No.38/2 and claimant No.8 Eraiah has proved his right, title and interest to the extent of 3 acres out of the acquired land and thereby, entitled to receive the compensation accordingly.
The said Veeranna has also examined himself as P.W.2 in the said case.
Ex.D.3 is the certified copy of the orders in O.S.No.5501/2022 wherein, the plaint was rejected which was filed by the daughter of Veeranna.
Ex.D.4 is the certified copy of the order in W.P.No.3135/2014(LA-BDA) dated 30.06.2015 between Sri.Veeranna Vs. State of Karnataka, BDA and Land Acquisition Officer.

Said Writ Petition is filed challenging the notification issued by the respondent BDA for formation of Gnanabharathi layout vide preliminary notification and final notification and published in official gazette on 03.03.1994.

Taking on / 27 /
O.S.No.1208/2023 record the memo filed by the learned counsel for the petitioner, the petition was dismissed as withdrawn.

8 24.
In the cross-examination, he admits 5 acres 30 guntas in Sy.No.38/2 of Nagadevanahalli village initially belonged to HosamaneChikkanna.

He denies the suggestion that, under the partition the son of HosamaneDoddaiah i.e., Veeranna received 2 acres 30 guntas of land and further denies the suggestion that, the said properties are carved and 2 acres 30 guntas belongs to Veeranna.
He admits in the suit filed by him against BDA, / 28 / O.S.No.1208/2023 he has restricted for 3 acres of land.
He admits BDA has filed the statement stating they have acquired the entire extent of Sy.No.38/2 and they have deposited the amount in LAC No.29/1996.
He admits the property acquired by BDA is not developed and it is lying vacant.
But, denies the suggestion that Veeranna has formed sites in 2 acre 30 guntas in Sy.No.38/2 and sold the sites to the plaintiff and his father.
He denies the suggestion that, the plaintiff is owner in possession of suit schedule properties.
25. Heard the counsel for the plaintiff and defendant and perused the records.
It is well settled principle that the plaintiff has to prove his case on his own strength and cannot be rely on the weakness of the / 29 / O.S.No.1208/2023 defendant.
There is no dispute that, the vendor of the plaintiff i.e., Veeranna is the son of HosamaneDoddaiah.
The plaintiff claims that he and his father has purchased the suit schedule properties from Veeranna under registered sale deed under a GPA dated 08.06.1990.
For the reason best known to the plaintiff, the said GPA is not produced before this court.

On perusal of Ex.D.1 and 2, the judgment and award passed in LAC No.28/1996 the Hon'ble LAC court while determining the title of the parties i.e., claims with reference to land acquired by BDA in Sy.No.38/2 has held that, claimant No.5 i.e., the vendor of the plaintiff does not have title, right and interest in any portion of the Sy.No.38/2 and the title of the grandmother of the defendant was confirmed to an extent of 2 acre 27 guntas.

Further, Ex.D.4 the copy of order passed in W.P.No.3135/2014 (LA-BD) which is filed by the vendor of / 30 / O.S.No.1208/2023 the plaintiff against the State Government , BDA and Land Acquisition Officer, he himself has challenged the preliminary and final notification issued by BDA on 02.02.1989, 19.01.1994.
However, he himself by filing a memo has got the petition dismissed as withdrawn.
It implies that the vendor of the plaintiff had no title, interest and possession of any portion of Sy.No.38/2.
When the said property is alleged to be sold to the plaintiff and his father H.Panchanna.

When the vendor of the plaintiff had executed Exs.P.1 to 14 in favour of the plaintiff and his father, the entire portion of the said land was already acquired by BDA under preliminary notification dated 19.01.1989, 26.01.1989 and 02.02.1989 and the final notification on 19.01.1994 and the possession was taken over on 31.01.1995.

It establishes that on the execution of the sale deeds Exs.P.1 to 14, Veeranna had no right, title, / 31 /
O.S.No.1208/2023 interest to execute any sale deeds in favour of the plaintiff and his father.
Further, P.W.1 himself in the cross admit that, BDA has acquired the land and formed layout.
Further, mere producing the revenue records i.e., RTC, tax paid receipts does not establish the title over the suit schedule properties.

As per the above said reasoning when Veeranna had no title over 3 acre 20 guntas of land, the plaintiff and his father has not received any title, interest and possession over the suit schedule properties under the alleged sale deeds dated 05.07.2013.

Hence, the plaintiff has failed to prove that he has become absolute owner of item Nos.1 to 4 as per registered Sale Deed dated 05.07.2013 and his father had purchased item Nos.5 to 14 under registered Sale Deeds dated 05.07.2013.
Based on above said reasoning, I answer Issue Nos.1 and 2 in the negative.

Nandish M P vs Kumar on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96817976/
9 / 32 / O.S.No.1208/2023 26.
Issue No.3 :
- As per the findings in the Issue Nos.1 and 2, BDA had acquired the land on 31.01.1995 and the plaintiff has not acquired valid title under the Sale Deeds dated 05.07.2013.
Further, P.W.1 admit in cross that, BDA has acquired the lands and formed layout.
Hence, the plaintiff failed to prove that he is in possession and enjoyment of suit schedule properties.
With this observation, I answer Issue No.3 in the negative.

27. Issue No.4 : - When the plaintiff as per the findings in issue Nos.1 to 3 failed to prove title and possession of suit schedule properties, the question of alleged interference by the defendant does not arise for consideration.
With this observation, I answer Issue No.4 in the negative.
Issue No.5 : - Based on the findings on Issue Nos.1 to 4, plaintiff is not entitled for declaration relief and permanent injunction relief as sought in the suit.
With this observation, I answer Issue No.5 in the negative.
29. ISSUE NO.6 : - Based on the findings on Issues Nos.1 to 5, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The suit filed by the plaintiff seeking declaratory relief and consequential relief of permanent injunction is hereby dismissed with costs.
Draw decree accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The suit is filed by the plaintiff to declare that the Judgment and Decree passed in O.S.No.10127/2015 dated 28.04.2017 by Hon'ble Addl. City Civil & Sessions Judge, Bengaluru is not binding on the plaintiff nor it is relating to the suit schedule properties and for permanent injunction restraining the defendant, his agents, servants or any persons claiming under him from interfering with plaintiff's peaceful possession and enjoyment of suit schedule properties .
After the demise of plaintiff's father, the plaintiff succeeded to the estate of his father and inherited item Nos.5 to 15 of suit schedule properties.
The defendant taking advantage of the decree, on 14.02.2023 dictated the plaintiff to demolish the watchman shed and to remove the fence built over the suit schedule properties and threatened that he would interfere with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of / 8 / O.S.No.1208/2023 plaintiff's properties.
The defendant again on 15.02.2023 along with some persons came near the suit schedule properties and interfered with the plaintiff's peaceful possession and enjoyment of the property and the plaintiff gave complaint to Kengeri Police Station.
The cause of action for the suit arose on 14.02.2023 and subsequently, when the defendant tried to dispossess the plaintiff and hence, prays for the reliefs as sought for.
Hence, the grandmother of the defendant Smt.Chikkamma was the absolute owner of 5 acre 30 guntas in Sy.No.38/2.
All the revenue records stood in her name.
After the death of Smt.Chikkamma, the defendant being the legal heir became the owner in possession of 5 acre 13 guntas and he is in lawful possession and enjoyment of the said land.
Further contend, Sy.No.38/2 was acquired by BDA in the year 1989 and upon the objections of the alleged vendor of the plaintiff's and others, the BDA had referred the matter under section 30, 31(2) of Land Acquisition Act in LAC 28/1996 before Hon'ble Addl. City civil judge,
Bengaluru.
In the said proceedings, the grandmother of the defendant Smt.Chikkamma appeared as claimant No.4 and the vendor of the plaintiff, Veeranna / 10 / O.S.No.1208/2023 appeared as claimant No.5.
In the said LAC proceedings after full fledged enquiry and after considering the evidence of the claimants, the Hon'ble court allowed the claim of grandmother of the defendant i.e.,
claimant No.4 and rejected the claim of other claimants including the claim of the vendor of the plaintiff and the said judgment and decree was passed on 06.11.2004 and no appeal has been filed against the said judgment and it has attained finality.
8.
In the said suit, the defendant appeared and filed application under Order VII Rule 11 of CPC and the plaint was rejected on merits vide order dated 23.05.2023.
The plaintiff is / 11 / O.S.No.1208/2023 claiming right over the suit property under Veeranna whose claim is rejected in LAC No.28/1996.
Hence, the plaintiff has not acquired any right, title and interest over the suit schedule properties and was never in possession and enjoyment of the same.
9. Further state, the defendant had filed W.P.No.14449/2019 against BDA challenging the acquisition proceedings on the ground that, he is in physical possession of the land and scheme of BDA lapsed due to non-development of acquired land and same is pending for consideration.
The defendant is in physical possession and enjoyment over the said land.
15. The plaintiff's case is that, he is purchased item Nos.1 to 4 from Veeranna S/o HosamaneDoddaiah under registered Sale Deed dated 05.07.2013 and the remaining item Nos.5 to 14 were purchased by his father H.Panchanna and after the death of his father, his mother and his sister executed registered Relinquishment Deed dated 21.08.2015 in respect of item Nos.5 to 14 in favour of the plaintiff and subsequently, the plaintiff is the owner in peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule properties.
The plaintiff has not acquired any valid right, title and interest in suit schedule properties and was never in possession of the same.
opennyai_summary.issue:
In the light of the aforesaid rival pleadings of the parties, the following issues have been framed by my predecessor in office :
(1) Whether the plaintiff proves that he became the absolute owner of item No.1 to 4 of the suit schedule site property by virtue of registered sale deeds dated 05.07.2013 ?

4
(2) Whether the plaintiff proves that his deceased father had purchased item No.5 to 14 of suit schedule property through registered sale deeds dated 05.07.2013 and after the death, he had succeeded to the said property ?
(3) Whether the plaintiff proves his lawful possession over suit schedule property as on the date of the suit ?
(4) Whether the plaintiff proves the alleged interference of the defendant ?
(5) Whether the plaintiff is entitle for the relief of declaration and permanent injunction ?
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The defendant has claimed right only in 3 acres in O.S.No.10127/2015 against the BDA as such, the vendor of the plaintiff had title over the 2 acres 30 guntas of land.
Further argued / 17 / O.S.No.1208/2023 that, the plaintiff has not produced the GPA copy to show the plaintiff had valid title over the suit schedule properties.
The revenue documents even though stands in the name of plaintiff's it does not confer title to the plaintiff.
Hence, prays for dismissal of the suit.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The land was acquired by the BDA for formation of Gnanabharathi layout and the preliminary notification was published on 19.01.1989, 26.01.1989 and 02.02.1989 and final notification was / 25 / O.S.No.1208/2023 published on 19.01.1994.
It is well settled principle that the plaintiff has to prove his case on his own strength and cannot be rely on the weakness of the / 29 / O.S.No.1208/2023 defendant.
On perusal of Ex.D.1 and 2, the judgment and award passed in LAC No.28/1996 the Hon'ble LAC court while determining the title of the parties i.e., claims with reference to land acquired by BDA in Sy.No.38/2 has held that, claimant No.5 i.e., the vendor of the plaintiff does not have title, right and interest in any portion of the Sy.No.38/2 and the title of the grandmother of the defendant was confirmed to an extent of 2 acre 27 guntas.
It implies that the vendor of the plaintiff had no title, interest and possession of any portion of Sy.No.38/2.
When the said property is alleged to be sold to the plaintiff and his father H.Panchanna.
When the vendor of the plaintiff had executed Exs.P.1 to 14 in favour of the plaintiff and his father, the entire portion of the said land was already acquired by BDA under preliminary notification dated 19.01.1989, 26.01.1989 and 02.02.1989 and the final notification on 19.01.1994 and the possession was taken over on 31.01.1995.
It establishes that on the execution of the sale deeds Exs.P.1 to 14, Veeranna had no right, title, / 31 /
O.S.No.1208/2023 interest to execute any sale deeds in favour of the plaintiff and his father.
Further, mere producing the revenue records i.e., RTC, tax paid receipts does not establish the title over the suit schedule properties.
